summary.headline: 20 Microns Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 14.8% YoY and PAT about 16.6%, with EBITDA margin steady near 12%.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of resilience and strategic transition despite weak paints demand, monsoon disruption and geopolitical pressure. Q4 revenue grew about 14.8% YoY and about 21.5% QoQ, led by paints and polymer/rubber recovery and pre-buying linked to the war situation. EBITDA grew 9.6% YoY to Rs 31.8 crore with margin stable near 12%, and PAT rose 16.6% YoY on lower finance cost. Management withheld broad FY27 revenue and margin guidance, but reiterated a medium-term plan of about 18% revenue CAGR and 200-250 bps margin expansion, subject to geopolitical stability.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 31.8 crore (stated as EBITDA grew to 31.8 crore)
growth stated as 16.6% YoY and 17.6% (second figure not clearly labelled)

segments.name: Paints and coatings
segments.commentary: Above 46% of revenue; management said paints revenue was flat YoY in FY26, with no decline.

segments.name: Polymer, rubber, plastics, inks, construction chemicals
segments.commentary: Management named these as growth areas beyond paints; new products for tyres, petrochemicals and cosmetics were commercialised in FY26. Construction chemicals remain small-volume at present.

segments.name: Industrial applications (five-year view)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from Rs 613 crore in FY22 to Rs 954 crore in FY26, about 12% CAGR; EBITDA rose from Rs 79 crore to Rs 123 crore.

guidance_outlook: No broad FY27 revenue or margin guidance given; management said it did not find it suitable amid current uncertainty, and denied withdrawing guidance.
Medium-term plan (three years, conditional on stable economy): about 18% revenue CAGR, about 200-250 bps EBITDA margin expansion, RoCE of 18-20%.
Management expects growth to cross Rs 1,000 crore revenue in FY27 if demand improves in the next one to two months, mainly in the second half.
Most Rs 100 crore capex projects targeted for completion by FY30; RoCE of about 20% expected by FY30 if timelines hold; plans may be modified or deferred given geopolitics.
Malaysian plant to be commissioned within about 12 months, with operations starting early in the next financial year.
Net working capital requirement in FY27 expected to stay at FY26 levels; no customer payment delays identified as of the call.
capex_capacity: Rs 100 crore capex plan covering capacity expansion in mining and infrastructure, sustainability, R&D, AI-linked processes and backward integration; about 40% allocated to Malaysian operations.
Funding: domestic capex mainly from internal accruals; Malaysian entity targeted at about 70:30 equity-to-debt (30% debt).
Malaysian limestone mines have started operating; plant construction takes at least 12 months.
Sievert JV: phase 1 established in recent months; phase 2 expected to go live in the next few months; full impact expected by year-end FY27.
Doffner JV is already contributing to the overall picture.
Raw materials: about 30% sourced from company mines, about 70% from external sources (domestic and imports); some domestic mines under environmental clearance.
Automation, renewable energy (solar, hybrid, wind) and new-age milling processes planned to cut power costs; automation to be taken up within the three-year capex plan.
demand_pricing: Demand recovered from January 2026, with a stable uptrend in February; Q4 also saw customers building inventory amid the war situation.
Management said demand is expected to be volatile in the near term; customer offtake expectations are updated every few weeks to months rather than set by long-term contracts.
Cost pass-through: rising fuel, gas, freight, raw material and forex costs are passed on case by case, with a lag of days to weeks.
Gas and fuel supply is tight but production is running at planned levels as of the call; multiple sources are in use.
Market share ranges from 10% to 30% depending on product; main competitors include international and domestic players, with a list to be sent later.
Management said it was unclear whether April to June will be the highest-revenue quarter, given current weaker demand.
New products add about 4-5% of revenue annually, partly through upgrades that replace older products.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 100 crore capex be funded, and what is the debt-equity mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic capex is mainly from internal approvals and accruals; the Malaysian entity is planned at about 70:30 equity to debt.

qa_highlights.question: Can PAT reach Rs 100 crore in FY27 and when will the capex be complete with what returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict given current conditions; capex is in place, with most projects by FY30 and RoCE of about 20% targeted by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance not given, and what is the revenue and margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it did not find broad guidance suitable amid uncertainty; it hopes for growth to cross Rs 1,000 crore in the second half if demand improves in the next month or two.

qa_highlights.question: What are free cash flow and the revenue split between new and legacy products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 free cash flow was about Rs 42.28 crore (as stated by the CFO; the call referred to the previous year). New products contribute about 4-5% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is supply chain or fuel cost a risk, and are costs passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel, gas, forex, freight and raw material costs are rising; increases are passed on to customers case by case, with a lag of days to weeks. Production is at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company debt-free aspirational, and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to be debt-free eventually and will share timelines later; FY27 working capital is expected to stay at FY26 levels with no payment delays seen.

risks_watch: Geopolitical situation: fuel, gas, forex and freight cost pressure, and possible government restrictions on gas supply; management said capex plans could be modified or deferred.
Demand volatility in paints and coatings, with near-term demand described as weaker and FY27 guidance withheld.
Malaysian plant commissioning (about 12 months away) and Sievert JV phase 2 timing.
FY26 revenue of Rs 953 crore must step up to Rs 1,000 crore or more in FY27 for the stated growth path to hold.
Q4 revenue partly driven by pre-buying linked to war-related fears, which may not repeat.
Rising PAT target of Rs 100 crore in FY27 was not confirmed by management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term strategy and balance sheet, but cautious and at times evasive on FY27 numbers, citing the geopolitical situation, with explicit caveats that plans may change. Several answers were incomplete due to call audio issues.
key_quotes: Our hundred crore CapEx equally nears about 16% of the current market capitalization.
Well, it's very difficult to predict as of now because of the current situations and we don't know for how long these current situations are going to last for.
So anywhere in the early next financial year is when we are expecting the operation operations to show some light.
